nodes.label: Assistant Mode
nodes.rationale: Repository analysis is read-only unless the user explicitly requests implementation.

nodes.label: Implementor Mode
nodes.rationale: Code changes must be explicitly authorized and limited to the requested task.

nodes.label: Manual Verification Policy
nodes.rationale: Tests, linters, formatters, type checks, builds, and runtime validation are reserved for the developer.

nodes.label: Bot Module Boundary Policy
nodes.rationale: Handlers remain thin, services own business rules, repositories own persistence, and bot modules consume platform infrastructure.

nodes.label: Secret Management Policy
nodes.rationale: Credentials, Fernet keys, and tunnel tokens must stay out of version control and production secrets belong in a secret manager.

nodes.label: Modular Monolith Architecture
nodes.rationale: Multiple independently developed bots share one deployable application, one database, infrastructure, and transactions while retaining explicit module boundaries.

nodes.label: Update Idempotency and Retry Leases
nodes.rationale: Updates are keyed by bot and update IDs, claimed under processing leases, bounded by attempt count, and deduplicated to prevent concurrent duplicate handler execution.

nodes.label: Bot Module Contract
nodes.rationale: Modules own bot-specific routing and domain behavior but must not duplicate platform identity, session, credential-validation, or HTTP-client responsibilities.

nodes.label: Global Identity and Per-Bot Membership
nodes.rationale: A Telegram identity is global, while role, status, locale, metadata, and membership are isolated by bot.

nodes.label: Versioned Per-Bot User State
nodes.rationale: State is keyed by bot-user membership and guarded by compare-and-swap versions to prevent cross-bot leakage and silent lost updates.

nodes.label: Automatic User Registration
nodes.source_location: User Identity and Isolation > Automatic registration

nodes.label: Encrypted Per-Bot Credentials
nodes.rationale: Each bot token and webhook secret is encrypted in PostgreSQL with a rotatable Fernet key ring rather than stored as a global plaintext environment secret.

nodes.label: Trusted Bot Module Discovery
nodes.rationale: Only direct packages under the trusted app.modules namespace are imported, and HTTP path values are never interpreted as import paths.

nodes.label: Webhook Synchronization
nodes.rationale: Webhook configuration is changed only when the desired URL or locally stored HMAC fingerprint differs, avoiding unnecessary Telegram API mutations while keeping secrets encrypted.

nodes.label: Degraded Health Model
nodes.rationale: A bot-specific startup failure degrades health without aborting unrelated bots, whereas a failed live database probe returns HTTP 503.

nodes.label: Redacted Structured Logging
nodes.rationale: Logs include operational identifiers but exclude request bodies, authorization headers, tokens, secrets, database URLs, and full Telegram message text.

nodes.label: Migration Before Application Startup
nodes.rationale: Both application services upgrade the Alembic schema before executing Uvicorn.

nodes.label: Health-Gated Service Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Application services wait for healthy PostgreSQL, and the tunnel waits for a healthy development application.

nodes.label: Root Compose Convention
nodes.rationale: The Dockerfile and Compose definition stay at repository root so docker compose up --build works without extra flags; the docker directory is reserved for deployment extensions.
